summary.title: Vector Database from Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a small in-memory vector database in Rust, add IVFFlat, NSW, HNSW and IVF-PQ indexes, and expose top-k vector search through SQL via DataFusion.
takeaways: Exact search compares a query with every stored vector; ANN indexes trade some result accuracy for speed.
How to expose a safe SQL top-k query over vectors by routing it to a vector index through a DataFusion optimizer rule.
How IVFFlat, NSW, HNSW and IVF-PQ differ in build cost, representation size, latency and recall.
How to benchmark ANN results against exact search using rank recall and latency on SIFT1M with Euclidean distance and k = 100.
summary.summary: This is a six-day hands-on course for systems and backend engineers, written as an online book. It builds an in-memory Arrow-backed vector table in Rust, starts with exact nearest-neighbor search, then adds IVFFlat, NSW, HNSW and residual IVF-PQ indexes. A DataFusion adapter routes safe SQL top-k queries to a vector index, and Day 6 compares all five indexes on SIFT1M. The course explicitly excludes embedding models, persistence, online updates, filtered search and GPU work, and it implements the indexes directly rather than calling an ANN library.
